tldr: The paper introduces MultiAgentBench, a comprehensive benchmark and MARBLE framework for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent systems across collaborative and competitive scenarios using novel milestone-based KPIs.
contributions: Introduction of MultiAgentBench, a benchmark evaluating LLM-based multi-agent systems across six diverse interactive scenarios capturing both collaborative and competitive dynamics
Introduction of the MARBLE (Multi-agent cooRdination Backbone with LLM Engine) framework supporting various communication topologies and reasoning strategies
Proposal of innovative evaluation metrics including milestone-based KPIs, structured planning/communication scores, and a dedicated competition score
Demonstration of emergent social behaviors in multi-agent coordination
methods: The authors developed the MARBLE framework with three core modules: an Agent Graph Module that structures inter-agent relationships as directed triples, a Cognitive Module maintaining agent personas and reasoning strategies, and a Coordination Engine orchestrating execution. They designed a benchmark with task-oriented scenarios (research, Minecraft building, database error analysis, coding) and competitive scenarios (Werewolf, Bargaining), segmenting tasks into flexible milestones monitored by an LLM-based detector. They evaluated five models across four coordination protocols (star, chain, tree, graph) and four planning strategies (vanilla prompting, CoT, group discussion, cognitive self-evolving planning).
results: gpt-4o-mini achieved the highest average task score, with 84.13% in Research (vs. Meta-Llama-3.1-8B at 80.87% and 70B at 80.80%) and 65.10% in Coding. The graph protocol performed best among coordination protocols in the Research scenario. Cognitive planning improved milestone achievement rates by 3%. Meta-Llama-3.1-70B showed high coordination scores (75.00 in Minecraft) but very low task scores (0.21). Group discussion scored worst across all metrics. Increasing iterations beyond 7 caused coordination degradation, and increasing agents beyond 3 decreased overall KPI.
limitations: Coordination does not compensate for inherent task execution deficiencies (e.g., high CS but near-zero TS in some cases)
Group discussion underperformed, potentially due to overly large planning groups hindering effectiveness
Excessive iterations (beyond 7) lead to coordination degradation from communication overhead or conflicting directives
Increasing agent numbers beyond 3 decreases overall KPI due to increased collaborative complexity
No single metric fully captures model effectiveness; both task-specific abilities and coordination skills must be considered
